title: I Built This Algorithmic Quant Trading System About 2 Months Ago — IGN Is the Aggressive Signal
author: Nvoinxv
selftext:
I built this algorithmic quant trading system about 2 months ago and have been tweaking it since.

It's a rule-based/mathematical system written in Pine Script for short-term crypto trading, currently tuned for the 1-minute timeframe.

The main idea is pretty simple: use KAMA + Efficiency Ratio to determine the trend, Stochastic RSI to detect pullbacks, ATR for breakout detection, and Yang-Zhang volatility as a volatility measure.

There are 3 signal tiers:

PB = Pullback

Entry during a pullback within an established trend.

BRK = Breakout

Triggered when price crosses the ATR-based trailing stop.

IGN = Ignition

This is the aggressive one. It's designed to catch sudden momentum/expansion candles as early as possible. It requires the candle range to be significantly larger than ATR and the candle body to have enough directional strength.

So IGN is intentionally high-risk/aggressive. It can catch moves very early, but it can also generate more false signals compared to PB and BRK.

I recently tuned the system specifically for 1-minute crypto because the previous version was a bit too slow/reactive for that timeframe. The core KAMA, ATR, Ignition, and Yang-Zhang formulas were kept unchanged.

Would appreciate any feedback, especially on the logic itself rather than just the visual design.
